claims.text: Build-platform preheating during additive manufacturing reduces thermal gradients in AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing thermal gradients minimizes compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing thermal gradients lowers residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing thermal gradients limits defect formation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Lower segregation, residual stress, and defect formation improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to processing without platform preheating.
Platform preheating produces a more uniform thermal field during solidification.
Platform preheating reduces the temperature difference between the melt pool and surrounding material.
The reduced melt-pool temperature difference slows the cooling rate.
The reduced melt-pool temperature difference promotes more uniform solidification.
Slower cooling and more uniform solidification attenuate rapid compositional changes and thermal shock.
Attenuating rapid compositional changes and thermal shock lowers segregation, residual-stress accumulation, and processing-induced defect formation.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will have lower residual stresses than otherwise identically processed non-preheated specimens.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will exhibit less microstructural segregation and fewer defects than non-preheated specimens.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will exhibit greater ductility than non-preheated specimens.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi specimens will exhibit greater yield strength than non-preheated specimens.

The proposed effects are valid for laser powder-bed fusion within typical metallic-powder process windows but may not transfer to other processing methods or substantially different alloy compositions.
